title: Collective excitation-mediated transport in nanoscale Josephson junctions that exhibit quantum confinement
authors: Zhengyuan Liu, Sebastian Scherb, Werner M. J. van Weerdenburg, Daniel Wegner, Nadine Hauptmann, Alexander A. Khajetoorians
abstract: Quantum confinement can strongly modify transport through Josephson junctions. Here, we study local tunneling transport through nanoscale Josephson junction stacks in the Coulomb blockade regime, where the metallic layers exhibit strong vertical quantum confinement. We find that quasiparticle transport is strongly enhanced by a collective excitation mode intrinsic to the junction and localized in the isolated metallic overlayer. We quantify both the collective-mode energy and the Coulomb gap and show that both exhibit strong layer-dependent modulation, consistent with the modulation of the underlying quantum well states. We further investigate how the collective excitation responds to various perturbations, including mechanical motion and an applied magnetic field. Our results suggest that this collective mode is sensitive to quasiparticles near the Fermi level and may therefore provide an indirect probe of the superconducting state.
summary: This work uses advanced STM spectroscopy to study electron transport in quantum-confined Josephson junctions. The researchers find that the transport is significantly mediated by a collective excitation mode intrinsic to the junction structure. This mode's energy is highly sensitive to the underlying quantum well states and external fields, offering a novel probe into the superconducting state.
main_problem: The study investigates how collective excitation modes mediate quasiparticle transport in nanoscale Josephson junctions that are subject to strong vertical quantum confinement.
main_result: The transport is strongly enhanced by a collective excitation mode whose energy and the Coulomb gap both show strong modulation dependent on the quantum well states (QWS) of the metallic overlayer.
method: The research employs Scanning Tunneling Spectroscopy (STS) on nanoscale Josephson junction stacks, measuring differential conductance (dI/dV) under varying bias, magnetic fields, and tip-sample separation.
model_or_system: The physical system consists of Pb/NaCl/Pb Josephson junction stacks grown on Si(111). The analysis involves modeling the system in the Coulomb blockade regime, considering quantum confinement effects in the metallic overlayers.
key_observables: Coulomb gap strength, collective excitation energy ($\epsilon$), Quantum Well States (QWS) spectra, and the dependence of these features on overlayer thickness and magnetic field.
important_parameters: Temperature (1.2 K), magnetic field (up to 9 T), junction thickness (nanometer scale), and the ratio of charging energy to Josephson energy ($E_C \gg E_J$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the collective excitation may originate from phonons, plasmons, or polarons, and that the superconducting gap is masked by the strong Coulomb blockade.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate Coulomb gap spectra showing multi-gap structures, QWS spectra exhibiting bilayer oscillations, and plots detailing the dependence of the collective excitation energy on tip separation and magnetic field.
paper_structure: The paper systematically characterizes the QWS and Coulomb blockade features, demonstrating the enhancement of transport via a collective mode. It then investigates the dependence of this mode on external perturbations like magnetic fields and mechanical motion, comparing it to known vibrational excitations.
why_interesting: The coupling between electronic transport (quasiparticles) and collective excitations (plasmons/phonons) in confined superconducting systems is a key area for understanding energy dissipation and superconducting mechanisms in nanoscale devices.
